faces.f: The consciousness of Mat'Selesnya does not always spread in peaceful ways.
Wolf-riders of Selesnya apprentice from a young age. Each rider raises a wolf pup from birth to serve as a mount, hoping that one day the two will share the honor of guarding the Great Concourse.
A lawmage's runic script is an act of governance given form: legislation written directly onto the air itself.

"When the Simic say to take command of your life, we don't mean just your career."
—Vorel of the Hull Clade
Ral Zarek's brainstorms bring actual thunder and lightning.
A true Boros commando only calls for reinforcements so they can clean up the mess.
Leaders shape the minds of their allies. It takes a master to shape the minds of enemies.
Some see the world as a place of infinite wonder and knowledge. Some see it as an infinite dinner plate.
They fight for their home with more loyalty than any conscript.
Not the foulest or bloodiest act at Rix Maadi by a stretch.
Some of Orzhov's cruelest collectors remember their debtors by taste alone.
"Everyone deserves a day in court."
The rot farmer's first rite of passage is to craft a pair of work stilts.
When Selesnya needed a champion, Emmara put the ranks of her guild before herself—making her the perfect choice.
"Channeling the rage of the beast is the easy part. Explaining why you woke up with no memory in a pile of mangled lawmages—that's trickier."
One part mizzium, two parts elemental energy, eleven parts danger.
Golgari reclaimers resent the gorgons, begrudging the loss of so many fine nutrients locked away in stone.
Every soldier returns from battle changed: by hardship, by blood, by a glimpse of glory.

"All pilots and prototypes destroyed. Extensive collateral damage inflicted. Conclusion: flawless design."
—*Manual of Melek*

"We are the heart of the wild, the fire in its eyes, and the howl in its throat. Come, join the battle to which you were born."
—Kroshkar, Gruul shaman
The Dimir employ the spirits of Ravnica's ancient, nameless dead, guiding their malevolence toward selected victims.
Few among the Azorius have ever spoken with the sphinxes, but all have felt their influence.
"Welcome to my collection."
The devout sacrifice themselves to it hoping for escape from their debts to the guild, but many end up owing in the afterlife.

"Let him in. He's on the list."
—Olrich, Rakdos club owner

"The Obzedat have revived you with purpose. Don't squander their blessing."
—Teysa Karlov, Grand Envoy of Orzhov
Mirko Vosk hunted anyone with knowledge of the maze, draining the chances of the other guilds.

"Everything serves a purpose. Even you."
—Vorel of the Hull Clade

"We are all decaying, always in a state of near-death. One moment without breath and we begin to break down."
—Cevraya, Golgari shaman
"We have confiscated your spells as evidence. Once we conclude our investigation, you may petition to have them returned."

"You can always count on the Azorius to ruin a party."
—Massacre Girl
For the Gruul, bone-crushing rage is the first priority. Accuracy comes in a distant ninetieth.
The audience quickly realized a few things: it wasn't a magic trick, there wasn't candy in there, and they'd need new clothes.
"That must weigh heavily on your soul. Let me purge it for you."
Its victims become mindless lunatics. Conveniently, that's the first step in joining the Cult of Rakdos.

"We raised eelhawks to control the squidflies, then waspcrabs to prey on the eelhawks. Now what do we do with all these waspcrabs?"
—Gulistan, Simic biomancer
For the Rakdos, "suicidal charge" and "good showmanship" are one and the same.
"I run the maze alone, but I fight with the full might of the Legion."
As Trostani's influence grew, vitality spread through the Conclave—much to the other guilds' dismay.

"All that steel doesn't make them slower. It makes them bolder."
—Tajic, Blade of the Legion
"I used to hurl rocks and eat scraps of meat burned over a fire. Look at what I've become and tell me Simic does not hold infinite possibility."

"There is no time to remedy our enemies' ignorance. Blast it out of them."
—Aurelia
The Gruul seek unbounded strength. The Dimir deliver cruel irony.

"We learned something from the Simic. Unfortunately for them."
—Nefara, Dimir agent
Many Ravnicans think of nature as orderly groves and elf-tended rot farms. They haven't seen the Gruul wilds.
"Only the decadent think magic should be pristine and without cost."
Its three sides represent the Sova, judges and arbitrators; the Jelenn, scribes and elocutors; and the Lyev, lawmages and enforcers.

"In case of fire, treachery, citywide riot, political upheaval, or worldwide societal collapse, break glass."
—Cluestone inscription
It waits in the chill of the undercity, holding nameless secrets for those who dare to touch it.
Golgari mold collects whispers, intelligence that is later harvested by Jarad and his high chancellors.
Forgotten under rocks and vines, Gruul symbols mark the sites of primitive rituals where shamans once chanted to the wild.
It holds within it an unsolvable riddle. A creative answer yields an invitation to the guild.
A symbol of power and wealth, the only commodities that matter to the Orzhov.

"Burn. Bleed. Enjoy."
—Cluestone inscription

"Break it if you must. The loss of one relic is nothing next to the value of enriching us all."
—Suniel the Woodwise
Simic symbols are among the most intricate and fragile, yet few vandalize them for fear of the strange lifeforms that might be released.
The Azorius symbol stares down like a great eye, reminding visitors of the watchful presence of Isperia and her lawmages.
It promises protection to those in need and proclaims a warning to any who would threaten Ravnican law.
In the cold corridors of the undercity, misinformation unfurls from Duskmantle like a spreading stain.
Every part of the gate was reclaimed from forgotten ruins and imbued with new purpose by the Swarm.
The scarred rubble around the gate is testament to past meetings of the Clans, summits that inevitably devolved into brawls.
Beyond lies the culmination of all Izzet projects, a grand experiment led by the dragon Niv-Mizzet himself.

"We do not believe in hiding our wealth in the shadows. This is Orzhov, and this is how we reward greatness."
—Teysa Karlov, Grand Envoy of Orzhov
Maze-runners who pass through the Rakdos gate leave behind their scruples and a significant amount of skin.
The Selesnya welcome all to help them heal the city's wounds. The price, however, is devotion to the guild and a selfless belief in Trostani.
Simic biomancers don't concern themselves with guarding a gate. Their ever-present creations are enough to ward off trespassers.

"As peace should be—gentle yet unstoppable."
—Augustin IV
"Before the first stone was laid or the first elf-child born, the power of the nephilim was gathering. Let that power be spread by my hands."
Flesh can be tempered by spellcraft and forged ever stronger by the hammers of foes.
Her enemy's strength is her own.

"We thought the clouds had moved from the night sky. Then the night sky moved, and the horizon grew wings."
—Josuri

"No doubt the arbiters would put you away, after all the documents are signed. But I will have justice *now*!"
—Alovnek, Boros guildmage
Confront her, and feel the hooves of her steed. Ignore her, and feel the sting of her arrow.

The magic of the Guildpact gives aegis to the spirits pressed into its service. Upon entering the afterlife, they find new focus and are charged with defending the Guildpact against those who would see it broken.
"This aura threatens the sanctity of your soul. Wrenching it free won't be easy on either of us. If you're ready, we'll begin."
The Haazda shield is broad, protecting both the free and the guilded.
Some sky steeds break from the thundering herd to ride free on the open winds.
Properly honored dead gain the peace of the grave and freedom from the call of the Ghost Quarter.
In death, as in life, they protect the Grand Arbiter from exposure to contrary points of view.
"Life is fleeting, and so is death. Only the oath is eternal."
"As my father taught, 'Training will raise your shield to the blow, but courage fills the gaps the shield leaves open.'"
Its pulsating cry shatters bonds of iron, granite, and servitude.
While the soldier dreams, the eyes stand watch.
"You will do the thinking for the both of us!"
Every culture has its unlucky numbers. In a city where you're either alone, in a crowd, or being stabbed in the back, two is the worst number of all.
He unmakes the world in his own image.
"I could see in the other mage's eyes that he'd thought of it too. Then it became a race to exploit the knowledge first."
The Rakdos are unique in designing torture equipment they can operate while "suffering" alongside their victims.
To the Rakdos, the fun is in the shakedown. The loot is usually discarded.
There came a rush, a sudden fire in the mind. Then the two saw only the sooty fog of madness, heard only the crackling of their last thoughts burning away.
They knock 'em dead, with or without the punch line.
Like a vulture's scalp, the face of a drekavac is oily and hairless. The filth and disease of its carrion diet slip off its blood-slick skin.
Guilds often exterminate those who saw or knew too much. Some vindictive souls retain their knowledge, using it in the afterlife to crush the guilded and the vile bargain that gives them power.

"All dead move to the hollow rhythm of necromancy."
—Savra

"I call them 'Poke' and 'Prod.'"
—Chagrach, Rakdos cursemage

"Please tell me I'm hallucinating. I'd rather be crazy than here."
—Gorev Hadszak, Wojek investigator
"All ends in obliteration—love in hatred, life in death, and light in empty darkness."
They cut the stitches and give her sips of her brew. Then they sew her up again, and she's back to stirring.
An ogre's poisonous stench is like fine Kashkaval cheese to the noses lowest to the ground.

"A basilisk's gaze is effective, but disposing of physical remains is a tiresome task. It's far more discrete to dissolve one's victim entirely."
—Szadek
A Rakdos party is a flop if anyone lives to talk about it.

"The victim bears the marks of the 'Ktozok Impaler'. . . but he was executed years ago!"
—Gorev Hadszak, Wojek investigator

"Nature's exceptions remind us not to think in absolutes. Just as the orchid blossoms on blackened stone, so does the gift of mana occasionally manifest in the undead."
—Bougrat, druid of the Cult of Yore

"Some images are so powerful that one glance burns them into your mind forever. Come, let us gaze on nothingness."
—Szadek

"I like a little entertainment with my dinner."
—Rakdos

"The forward flame-kin are popping. We have incoming!"
—Svar, Boros signaler
A flame-kin is always formidable, but feeding its fire with a sorcerous gift grants it the power to devastate armies.
Despite its diminutive name, Gnat Alley is the longest street in Ravnica. Mile after twisting mile, it threads its way among the broader, safer thoroughfares like a parasite.

"A quick step beyond oblivion lies a place so full of thoughts that it leaves no room for your own."
—Quyzl, chronarch prodigy
Dressed to kill.
"Start knockin' heads, boys, and don't stop 'til the ragamuffyn sings!"
A popular game among ogres is to see how many revolutions a head can make before it pops off.

"Rage, my servants. Our ancient power is renewed in blood."
—Rakdos

"If it breathes, it will burn."
—Rakdos pyromancers' creed
Something roams the killing places, sniffing the guilt of the slayers, stalking them on iron paws.
The taste of blood breaks down what little self-control the Rakdos possess.
He wages war wherever the wind carries him.
Razia, archangel of war, demands total commitment.

"Finally, a good use for an Azorius courthouse."
—Ghut Rak, Gruul guildmage

"It wags its tail when it's happy. It wags its tail when it's angry. Nope, there's no good time to be around a whiptail."
—Rugar, Leaguehall Infirmary patient

"This undemanding vegetation takes root in a mote of dust but grows incredibly quickly."
—Simic research notes

"An indrik's howl has destructive power much subtler than that of its crushing foot. The sound is mundane, but inaudible vibrations scatter and sunder magical contrivances."
—Simic research notes
His work determines who is remembered and who feeds the worms.

"Send a runner to Tin Street, and tell 'em the delivery has been . . . uh . . . held up."
—Bonmod, caravan rear guard

"Meat *and* eggs. We eat!"
—Borborygmos
Simic initiates begin their training as experimental subjects. Failures are flushed to the undersewers.

"Infused with autochthon blood for size and hellion cells for speed, the ragworm is perfect for clearing the undergardens of both rats and vagrants."
—Yolov, Simic bioengineer
A hydra tender's problem isn't having enough defenses but enough pots.

"Mizzium may be impervious to fire, but obviously certain other things can . . . modify its form."
—Ivos Koba, indrik handler
"It takes more than swift feet and dark shadows to slip by me unnoticed."
The most successful of Simic creations is cytoplasm, a living, symbiotic substance that feeds off genetic rhythms and strengthens its host in return.

"Show them to Razia and then to the Azorius sky marshals. We could create a fine bidding war—enough to fund the final stages of Project Kraj."
—Momir Vig
In her single metasphere are bound the records of every Ætheric transaction since the time of Azor.
With a steady diet of lawbreakers, Azorius griffins inevitably develop a resistance to the contraband magic that taints much of their prey.
Azorius military tactics, like their legal tactics, capitalize on delay and nullification.
Snaking remnants of nature directed by a body of thought and progress, the oracles embody all that is Simic.

"Though highly effective at reshaping flesh, these specially bred cytoplasts leave the subject reeking of omnibian mucus."
—Simic research notes
A thousand phobias sopped from the city and wrung from Rix Maadi as one.

"Of course it will grow beyond control—it was designed to choose its own evolution."
—Momir Vig
Lyzolda's pet rats eat better than the average citizen. In fact, they can usually be found eating the average citizen.
The Arbiter is a conduit of justice, a will so disciplined that it dispenses justice without ego or remorse.

"I must speak with Momir Vig about creating a water-spouting watchdog."
—Mathvan, Prahv scrollwarden
Few puppets are so willing.

"The best experiments are those whose successes replicate themselves."
—Yolov, Simic bioengineer
Sacrificial rites take place before an audience of cheering cultists, each begging to be the next on stage.

"This creature has hyperevolved chameleonic abilities. It no longer mimics its surroundings, instead forcing them to take on its form."
—Simic research notes
With one commanding word, the spell was put down and a fine collected for its casting.
The Rakdos make sure their victims remember their pain—or at least give up a little bit of their sanity in order to forget.

"Stay indoors, away from what seeps over the thresholds. This is the Demon's work, and only ill can come of it."
—Belko, owner of Titan's Keg tavern
"Great minds bleed alike."

"Our thrulls dissolve from the inside out in a matter of days. Shoddy work, but they're a scream while they last."
—Uzric, Rakdos guildmage

"We've bred out the shortcomings of the species' natural form and replaced them with assets of our own design."
—Momir Vig

"This world may not know peace, but in my presence you *will* know quiet."
—Augustin IV
Held aloft by metabolized magic, trygons are ravenous for sources of mystic fuel.
They're dying left and right.
Fruits of magic, roots in science.

"It is technically an ooze, but its lifespan measures only seconds. In that short time, its appetite for magic is extraordinary."
—Simic research notes
Rakdos festivals almost leave enough rubble in their wake to hide the bodies.
Such is the power of Rakdos that even his shadow takes on a cruel life of its own.

"Look beyond, to the vascular awareness that all life is a map to greater knowledge."
—Momir Vig, *Biomancy*, vol. I
When it takes forever to learn all the rules, no time is left for breaking them.
Most auramancers would have let the spikes hover just above the skin. Having the spikes rip through the skin from beneath was a touch added by Rakdos himself.
The maze-like design embodies the core of Azorius law—strict structure designed to test wills and stall change.

"Ooh, shiny! Let's pull off the chain and take her with us."
—Ukl, Gruul raider, last words
The vats are self-contained worlds, bubbling and churning with unnatural speed, boiling down eons of change into moments.
The stones hark back to an age before civilization, when the living earth blessed all who trod its untamed wilds.
Made of bone and boiled in blood, a Rakdos signet is not considered finished until it has been used as a murder weapon.

For the Simic Combine, its sigil serves not as an emblem of honor but as a trademark. Its familiar image on any biological commodity attests to superb craftsmanship, ingenious innovation, and higher cost.
Once tasted, the flavor of skullmead lingers in the throat, a secret brand of guilt for those who partake in forbidden pleasures.
Reluctant to meet face to face, the leaders of the ten guilds prefer to do official business through a go-between immune to bribes and threats.
Where wasted life cries out to be reborn.

"The unnatural pressures of life in this city are best withstood by lifeforms that adapt with unnatural swiftness."
—Momir Vig
Built on the very ground where the Ten signed the Guildpact, the tower is a monument to the past and a reminder of who holds power in the present.
Prahv, where much work is done to make sure nothing is accomplished.
Even miles away, if you put your ear to the sewer vents, you can hear the screams and the tempestuous laughter.

"This is the light of Avacyn. Even in her absence she offers us hope."
—Radulf, priest of Avacyn

"It may not look like much, but it's a good old door with strong wards. It'll hold."
—Olgard of the Skiltfolk

"Grab an axe and defend the gate! Your despair is an extravagance we can ill afford."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar

"I do believe your heresy will prove more difficult now that you have more pressing concerns."
—Bishop Argust
"It will take more than steel alone to purge this world of evil."
In the memories of those they lost lies the strength needed to defend their city.
"I wish my work could shelter everyone, yet I pray we are never so few that it does."
Some spirits mourn. Others terrorize.
The murdered inhabitants of Hollowhenge impart to the living the terror they felt in death.

"I trust myself to do my duty, even unto death. It's what comes after that I'm afraid of."
—Constable Visil, to Thalia

"Just fight without fear. Your soul is protected by the hand of Avacyn and will never submit to evil."
—Thalia, to Constable Visil

"When you're on watch, no noise is harmless and no shadow can be ignored."
—Olgard of the Skiltfolk

"Not even a roaring fire could thaw the chill it put in my heart."
—Vonn, geist-trapper

"I never had the nerve to open that bottle. I'll bet you're wishing right now you hadn't been so curious yourself."
—Old Rutstein

"May angels carry him into the Blessed Sleep with dreams of sunlit days and moonless nights."
—Tomb inscription of Saint Raban
When angels despair, what hope can remain for mortals?
Cats prowl the corridors of Avacyn's churches in search of devils or signs of their mischief.
It patrols the grafs for miles around Thraben, ensuring that the unhallowed do not wake for long.

"Valor is a currency of the living that serves us well."
—Cosper Lowe of the Silbern Guard
"Thraben is our home and I will not see it fall to this unhallowed horde."
"Swarms of the unhallowed claw at Thraben's gates! Do you still deny the end approaches?"
"Let them decry me for burning the dead. I'm not giving those ghoulcallers any more fuel for their madness."
Those who know the alleys and sewers of the Erdwal can disappear like smoke.
"Come, let me free you of the tyranny of thought."

"I can think of worse ways to go. On second thought, maybe not."
—Ludevic, necro-alchemist
The skifsang, seafarers of Nephalia, craft spells like other sailors craft nets—making them strong enough to snare even the deadliest catch.
"Wait . . . did you fellows hear something?"
"Pathetic. Let me show you how it's done."
Even the House of Galan, who takes the most scholarly approach to the mystic traditions, has resorted to exploring more primitive methods in Avacyn's absence.

"Beware the seagrafs just off the shore. These waters are filled with hungry geists looking for an easy meal."
—Captain Eberhart
"So many corpses, so little time."
A head is a needless encumbrance when muscle is all that's required.

"Keep one eye on the cliff road or you may fall to your death. Keep one eye on the sky or your death may fall on you."
—Manfried Ulmach, Elgaud Master-at-Arms

"Why do the dead remain among us? Where is Flight Alabaster to lead them home? Where is Avacyn?"
—Eruth of Lambholt
Nothing's more valuable than perfect timing.
Its screeching is the sound of you losing your mind.

"The veil between the living and the dead is so very thin that the whispers of the ancients can finally be heard."
—Amalric of Midvast Hall
Wounds of the flesh are easy to heal. Wounds of the mind may never be undone.
The body often twists and flails spasmodically as the spirit explores its new home.

"As you inject the *viscus vitae* into the brain stem, don't let the spastic moaning bother you. It will soon become music to your ears."
—Stitcher Geralf
Jenrik's tower is served by those who once sought to enter it uninvited.
Its last life is spent tormenting your dreams.
"I have been found worthy by this great house . . ."
". . . and for that I shall be eternally grateful."

"May you drink until you drown but never be sated."
—Odila, witch of Morkrut
What could be more irresistible than death?
The faint smell of cloves, the rustling of the wind, and a paralyzing descent into an airless, fathomless tomb.
"There was a time when our cages rang with wailing. Now only a handful of these whimpering fools remain."

"Here are some bones for you to choke on, dear brother!"
—Gisa, to Geralf

"Innistrad's ghoulcallers are talented enough, but let me show you what someone with real power can create."
—Liliana Vess

"The Blessed Sleep? Ha! Wake up my lovelies, there's work to be done!"
—Gisa, ghoulcaller of Gavony

"There are always fools who attempt to traverse Kruin Pass before sundown and every time they wind up in a race for their lives."
—Old Rutstein

"All the dead sleep lightly here, no matter how refined their beds may be."
—Grafdigger Wulmer
His twisted words entice the weak.
"The price is paid. The power is mine!"
The wreck hung on the jagged reef, each night disgorging more of its gruesome cargo.
It blindly marches on Thraben's gates, guided by its master's direful will.
Certain initiates into the Skirsdag cult take a vow of blindness, pledging obedience to none but demonkind.

"Let us remind these human cattle why they fear the shadows of this world."
—Aldreg, Skirsdag cultist
Linger on death's door and risk being invited in.

"Is it true the evil that people do follows them into death? Let's find out."
—Liliana Vess
He wields the full power of wrath unfettered by the sympathies of a soul.
Hers is an ancient form of necromancy, steeped in shamanic trance and ritual that few skaberen or ghoulcallers comprehend.

"There will come a day so dark you will pray for death. On that day your prayers will be answered."
—Minaldra, the Vizag Atum
The rising of the first full moon eliminated any doubt as to the horrible truth lurking within.
Being an alpha means proving it every full moon.
Succession is a matter of blood, and by blood it is often decided.
Every now and then, a devil's prank can give you a good idea.
It is the demon's mark, an infernal claim on the flesh of the guilty.
Savage vampires lurk in the Erdwal's network of passageways where prey is plentiful and easy to catch.
"Avacyn has abandoned us! We have nothing left except what we can take!"
"I drink of those who are worthy of my palate. The rest I burn."
Masters of the sword know the blade is not the only weapon at their disposal.
Devils infiltrated the lower levels of Thraben Cathedral, making cracks in load-bearing pillars and setting fire to precious archives.
Their language may be a cacophonous agglomeration of chittering snorts and mad barking, but the message they send is all too clear.

"Behind every devil's mayhem lurks a demon's scheme."
—Rem Karolus, Blade of the Inquisitors
He tried to live far from those he could hurt . . .
. . . but the monster within was a tireless hunter.
"Mortals practice swordplay for a few decades at best. How can they ever attain the exquisite mastery that eternity has to offer?"
"What use is a stake or holy symbol in the hands of a coward?"
"Tovolar, my master. Gather the howlpack, for the Hunter's Moon is nigh and Thraben's walls grow weak."

"Their hearts beat, their lungs draw breath, and they have one true form. I count them as allies of the living."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar
"Do not speak of this to the elders. They look unfavorably upon my indulgences."

"The wolves of our valley are bred to detest the scent of ghouls. For centuries they have kept our estates clear of such carrion."
—Olivia Voldaren

"Your fields will turn as black as a ghoul's tongue and fire shall be your only harvest."
—Minaldra, the Vizag Atum

"You must shatter the fetters of the past. Only then can you truly act."
—Rem Karolus, Blade of the Inquisitors
Devils redecorate every room with fire.
The skathul, spirits consumed by revenge, fester and seethe while looking for weak minds to assault.

"The wolves turned on us and a chill swept over me. The pack had a new leader."
—Alena, trapper of Kessig

"Your veil's curse won't stop me, deathmage. I have taken down countless night hunters and this dark plane is not big enough for you to hide."
—Garruk Wildspeaker, to Liliana Vess
Silent as winter snow, it seeks wild places unspoiled by the walking dead.
Cast out by his village, he now takes grim offense at refugees who seek shelter in his forest.
Feeling abandoned by Avacyn, some Kessigers turned to the pagan rituals of their ancestors.
It uproots entire fengrafs to add to its twisted frame.
As the creatures of the night closed in on humanity, Innistrad's primeval forces stirred, as though waking to watch the slaughter.

"Nothing in nature goes to waste, not even the rotting corpse of a good-for-nothing, blood-sucking vampire."
—Halana of Ulvenwald
In a world of monsters, it's the stuff of nightmares.

"Werewolves are an unholy mix of a predator's instinct and a human's hatred."
—Alena, trapper of Kessig
Its silk is highly prized, but then again, so is your life.

"Be wary of the seemingly gentle souls. The weak here were slaughtered long ago."
—Rem Karolus, Blade of the Inquisitors
"My village's fear drove me into the wild . . ."
". . . and I will bring the fury of the wild back to my village."
The Somberwald is her domain, and she has yet to hear an acceptable excuse for trespassing.
Geists of the hanged often haunt the tree on which they died.

Out chasing bears
—Kessig expression meaning "died in the woods"
As their villages fell to werewolves, fleeing refugees discovered they too had remarkable survival instincts.

"If you think you've killed one, guess again."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar
Otto the Hunter was filled with many grand ambitions. The snake was filled only with Otto.
The Ulvenwald makes no allowances for youth. Today's newborn is either tomorrow's hunter or tomorrow's lunch.
Though its mind has long since rotted away, it wields a sword with deadly skill.
Dead or alive, true leaders can inspire an entire army.
Wracked and warped with anguish, it obsessively seeks out other souls to hoard within its eternal prison.
"Your blood is quite pleasing. A pity there's not enough for both of us."
Fusing intelligence with the power of undeath requires inspiration of the darkest kind.

n: Huntmaster of the Fells // Ravager of the Fells

faces.f:
"No longer can we allow our human populations to be mindlessly slaughtered by ghouls. Slay all who trespass."
—Runo Stromkirk

n: Chalice of Life // Chalice of Death

faces.f: The sweet taste of hope's promise.
The bitter taste of life's only certainty.

n: Elbrus, the Binding Blade // Withengar Unbound

faces.f: Those who grasp its hilt soon hear the demon's call.
There are not enough lives on Innistrad to satisfy his thirst for retribution.

"If you wind up in one of mine, you can be sure as silver it will be your last."
—Grafdigger Wulmer

"Steel in the heart, silver in the bow."
—Wolfhunter's creed

"Our world is vast, but Thraben is its heart. The cathedral must stand even if the hinterlands are lost."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar

"I love what they've done with the place."
—Liliana Vess
A ghoulcaller's playground.

"For centuries my creation kept this world in balance. Now only her shadow remains."
—Sorin Markov

"Open the gates, and bid them enter."
—Lim-Dûl, the Necromancer

"Will not the mountains quake and hills melt at the coming of the darkness? Share this vision with your enemies, Lim-Dûl, and they shall wither."
—Leshrac, Walker of Night

"Leshrac, my liege, grant me the power I am due."
—Lim-Dûl, the Necromancer

"Serve me, and live forever."

The best cure for a big ego is a little failure.
Those who forget the horrors of the past are doomed to re-meet them.

"Don't worry. I'm not going to deprive you of all your secrets. Just your most precious one."
—Liliana Vess
A grave is the safest place to store ill-gotten treasures.
It *is* the thing that goes bump in the night.
In life, the nantuko study nature by revering it. In death, they study nature by disemboweling it.
To the novice necromancers, it looked exactly like a regular human grave.

"We had years to prepare, while they had mere minutes."
—Kerrick, sleeper agent
It was a profitable scheme, at least until the dead began to object.
Trained in the arts of stealth, royal assassins choose their victims carefully, relying on timing and precision rather than brute force.
The lamps on Wyndmoor Street snuff themselves at midnight and refuse to relight, afraid to illuminate what lies in the darkness.
True power is achieved through blood and sweat. But mostly blood.

Kicking the warren
—Argivian expression meaning "causing trouble"
Embermages aren't well known for their diplomatic skills.

"For dim-witted, thick-skulled genetic mutants, they have pretty good aim."
—Sisay, captain of the *Weatherlight*
When you've got nothing, you might as well trade it for something else.
"I've got this under control! Probably!"
A mother only a child could love.
"Fools dig for water, corpses, or gold. The earth's real treasure is far deeper."
"I only had time to read half the spell, but I'm pretty sure this will work!"
"My, what a pretty little trick. At least you'll die with style."
The thunderhead that leads in the storm.
The undisputed master of the mountains of Shiv.
"Ready . . . uh . . . fire!"
"Nothin' beat surprise—'cept rock."
The hammer strikes. The Flame awakens.
As the world steeled itself for the New Phyrexian invasion, the heart of the Pinelands awoke, and a new maro-sorcerer strode forth to join the fight.
Sages whisper of an undiscovered natural paradise, a tropical island unspoiled by war.

"We are never without guidance, if we but seek it."
—Taaveti of Kelsinko, elvish hunter
The first explorers found Argoth a storehouse of natural wealth—towering forests grown over rich veins of ore.
She nurtures each flower from seed to blossom, and in return, they whisper secrets only she can hear.
Its blood is life. Its body is growth.

"Bright spores coalesced in empty air. Seedlings burst through barren soil. Genesis had arrived."
—*Scroll of Beginnings*
"Humans bring nothing but suffering and deceit. They are not welcome in my forest."
"My mind has changed. My strength has not."
From the cracks in the stone, she reads stories of the past. From the swirling vines, she glimpses visions of the future.
"I'll call you Reginald, and you're Mimi, and you're Tank, and you're Bobo..."
In the treetops, unseen by many, lurks chittering, skittering death.

"Here in Fyndhorn, where Freyalise's power is strongest, the forest has its own opinion."
—Laina of the Elvish Council
"All of us, from the tiny leaf-mite to the towering baloth, are vital threads in the weave of life."
"Your presumption is your downfall."
Tormented by her own existence, Karona turned her wrath on the world that had birthed her.

"Don't you agree that mogg intellects are improved by zombification?"
—Lord Dralnu
A heart of light and a soul of darkness cannot coexist.

"Don't be silly. Panthers don't hunt in packs!"
—Jego, disgraced archdruid
The dwarves call their quicksilver techniques "improvisational weaponsmithing."
"Step aside, weakling, or I'll swat you like the bug you are."
Anything sent into a plagued world is bound to come back infected.

"All the power of a maro-sorcerer, all the mindless fury of a pitlord. He is a perfect servant."
—Geyadrone Dihada
"Yavimaya is one being—one vastness of rippling leaves, one deepness of roots, and one chatter of animals—of which I am one part."
"Nothing is too broken to mend."
Her wits are sharp, but her blades are sharper.
Zur remained aloof from Terisiare's suffering, intent only on his own perfection.
"Not so scary when you can't squeeze through the air ducts, are you?"
Its lock changes to fit each key.
A Thran relic, it has spent ten thousand years doing absolutely nothing.

"This little prize will cover your head, your spells, your bets, and your behind!"
—Pashad ibn Asim, Suq'Ata trader
In fire there is the spark of chaos and destruction, the seed of life. In ice there is perfect tranquility, perfect order, and the silence of death.
The crowd laughed heartily at the fool's performance, until his hat laughed back.

"Urza's machines have a splendid habit of excavating themselves."
—Rona, disciple of Gix
In a single blinding flash, Yawgmoth was obliterated, and Urza could finally rest.

"What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?"
—Jhoira, master artificer

"It has been my honor to improve on Thran's original design. Perhaps history will remember me in some small part for my work."
—Urza, in his apprenticeship
Even after thousands of years, the wondrous creations of the Thran guarded the lost empire's secrets with single-minded devotion.
Dominaria's most extravagant crypt nevertheless holds an empty grave.

"What's got three legs and three heads and wants to kill us? That's not a riddle!"
—Jayeen, Fallaji scout
It was the explorers' only tether to reality.
From concept to paper to reality.

"Our recruitment drives are bringing in fewer fresh troops every day. We need a new strategy."
—Urza, to Tawnos
The sunlight falls pristine on the temple at Epityr, softened by the remembered shadows of angelic saviors' wings.

"Our ancestors brought down a Phyrexian portal ship, then built our town on its hull. We're pretty proud of that."
—Alene of Riverspan
Serra's blessing lies strongest upon Sursi, where her holy chapels are untouched even as evil encroaches.

"We have inherited the mysteries of the Thran, but few of the answers."
—Jhoira

"They never found the body of young Josu, or that of his murderous sister."
—"The Fall of the House of Vess"
Wisdom is a precious heirloom to be passed down faithfully from each generation to the next.
An angel among angels, she carries the hopes of the world skyward.
"I could do this all day."
A single glimpse was enough to compel Captain Velkarne to lay down his sword and take up the poet's quill.
Each side prayed for the gods to smite the other. In the end, all their prayers were answered.

"Don't be silly, Grandfather. If the tides were caused by some monster drinking the ocean, wouldn't more ships go missing?"
—Leda, Vodalian youth
"Weren't you ever taught that it's rude to interrupt?"

"May Svyelun's waves drown your memory."
—Traditional merfolk curse
Wisdom is a well that never runs dry. It offers the most to those with the deepest thirst for knowledge.
There's lots of time like the present.
"You forfeited any right to mercy the moment you challenged me."

"Oh, don't worry about that one. I'm saving him for later."
—Liliana Vess

"Leave no survivors. Let the other worlds see what befalls those who attempt to resist the might of Phyrexia."
—Sheoldred

"Of course we can squeeze in a few more! It's not like corpses need personal space."
—Orson, cemetery baron
Most of the spirits that haunt Urborg were once ordinary people, even children, twisted beyond recognition by the swamp's corrupted mana.
Wisdom is a throne, a seat of power that only the strong are worthy to occupy.

"If you look past the giant claws, nasty teeth, and horrible breath, they're actually kind of cute."
—Shanna Sisay
"What's the worst that could happen?"
"Pyromancers are cowards who look no further than the flickering flame on the surface. I alone have the courage to dig to the true power that roils beneath."
No reinforcements. Nowhere to retreat. Nothing to lose.
"You with the red shirt! You're up next."

"I have never before felt so unwelcome in a forest."
—Jolrael
Its brilliant plumage painted streaks of color across a sky long darkened by war.
"Come, come, my hungry little friends! There's plenty for everyone."
Wisdom is a seed. Nurtured with patience and care, it will bear new fruit each season.
"It's a shame to see such potential wasted on petty evil. Let's correct that, shall we?"

"There is no sweeter sound than the deafening thunder of utter destruction."
—Kamahl, Pit Fighter
"Keep coming, weaklings! I'm just getting warmed up."
Perhaps things would have ended differently had its first gasping breath not been lost in the susurrus of shifting sands.

"They say the last owner cut out his own tongue, laughing the whole time. Superstitious drivel, but amusing, isn't it?"
—Hilde the Collector, last known words
Whether lives or precious artifacts, no price was too high to stop the Phyrexian invasion.
Optimally designed for agility, mobility, and lethality.

"In my dark moments, I think Urza may have been more of a father to his creations than he ever was to his own son."
—Tawnos

"Let the interlopers scurry like trapped rats until they exhaust themselves. They are no threat to us."
—Ith, High Arcanist
New Argive welcomed the kor people when they were displaced by the Rathi overlay. The kor repay that kindness with fierce loyalty.
To conserve ammunition, Jhoira modified ancient Thran artillery cannons to fire gouts of pure Shivan lava.
"A single light can hold back endless darkness."
Even he didn't know what he was until he felt his skin shifting and splitting, his mind overtaken by a chaos of whispers.

"Argivia's walls may run on powerstones, but its real power comes from its people."
—King Darien XLVIII
"This battlefield is an anvil, my mace a forging hammer . . . and you, Phyrexian scum, are the scrap metal that's about to be reshaped as I see fit."
"What lurks behind the faces of those you think you can trust?"
Argivia's clockwork fortifications are the stuff of legend, reminding all on Dominaria that ingenuity has saved them before and can do so again.
Serra's grace most often manifests as a healing touch, but it may also grant a merciful death.
Griffin flocks still patrol the skies above the Zhalfirin void, as though they are waiting for their old home to reappear.
"For Keld! For Benalia! For Dominaria!"

"Okay—you take the sixteen ragers and the hulk on the right. I'll take the ten defilers and the plaguelord on the left. Ready?"
—Danitha, to Radha
"What Phyrexia takes, the grace of Freyalise shall replenish."
"Phyrexians destroyed my village, but they cannot break my hope."

faces.f: In the fight to defeat Phyrexia, the courage of Benalish knights is matched only by that of their pegasus steeds.
When a Phyrexian agent cannot be killed, they must be contained.
Morale rarely survives the sudden appearance of a squad of Sursi skirmishers at an army's flank.
"Target acquired."
"Spiritual wholeness is not something you can give to yourself: it is attained only through the divine blessing of healing another."
Armed by Multani, she protected the forest from above.
"You are all part of my pride. As long as I live, I will protect you."
"Any one of us could be compromised," said Karn. "No one leaves until we know who can be trusted."

III — You may activate the loyalty abilities of planeswalkers you control twice this turn rather than only once.

faces.f: "Let them come. We will show them that Argivian steel is stronger than any Phyrexian metal."
As a young student, she dusted the shelves of Tolaria's great library. Now, she writes the books that line them.
Once the Society of Mishra took control, the Tolarian Academy at Lat-Nam became a haven for dark research.
The seafloor is strewn with the wreckage of Vodalia's would-be conquerors.
"You're not so special, Karn. Anything that has been assembled can be disassembled."

"Phyrexians pollute everything they touch, so the solution is simple: don't let them touch anything."
—Teferi

II — Target player mills four cards.
III — Exile target instant or sorcery card from your graveyard. Copy it. You may cast the copy.

faces.f: "I adore your outfit. It's so . . . rustic."
Some bad dreams stay with you forever.

"I've always made snap decisions. I'm just better at making the right ones now that I'm older and wiser."
—Teferi
The Tolarians had the maps, but only the Yavimayans knew how to read them.
"Ideas don't have to be big to be great."

"It's frustrating, isn't it, to be so weak and ineffectual? Don't worry, you'll be *compleat* soon enough."
—Rona

faces.f:
"Even if they're hunting for sleeper agents, who looks twice at a bird?"
—Rona
Homarid shells are adapted to the crushing pressure of the deepest depths; on land, their sturdiness seems supernatural.
Karn's creation allowed him to monitor events across Dominaria—and everything he saw worried him.
The already spectacular views from the towers of the College at Lat-Nam are sometimes enhanced by glimpses of drakes diving into the ocean to devour small sharks.

"The Talas pirates are motivated by money, so we paid them twice what they could steal from us to spy for us instead."
—Jhoira
Prized by wizards as a mobile scrying pool, it bears visions drawn from the depths of the sea.
Students fled with their research as Tolaria fell to the Phyrexians.
"If they don't drown, perhaps they'll rust."
Afterward, a number of treatises on sea serpent morphology were swiftly revised.

"There hasn't been an original thought on Vesuva in centuries."
—Emmest, Tolarian chronicler
"You're just one more pollutant to be removed from the sea."
Ships suspected of carrying Sheoldred's agents have a tendency to drift far off course as they sail through the Voda Sea.
Squee's orders basically came down to "attack the squishy parts."

"Since when is it cheating to give one side an unfair advantage?"
—Braids
Having encountered the bitter Phyrexian battleflies before, Squee knew not to bother eating them—or at least to stop after the fifth.

"Keep your distance. It may be broken, but it's far from benign."
—Stenn

"Steel may be more durable, but nothing channels the spite of the unjustly dead like bone."
—Braids

faces.f: The Phyrexians were as surprised as anyone to discover they still needed to breathe.

II — Search your library for a card, put that card into your hand, then shuffle. You lose 3 life.
III — Put target creature card from a graveyard onto the battlefield under your control.

faces.f: His eternal rest turned out to be more of a quick nap.

"There can be no mercy, no half measures. When facing Phyrexians, it's kill swiftly or die."
—Jodah
Windgrace's gladehunters hibernate in the quagmires of Urborg until the scent of Phyrexian technology awakens their hunger.
Jaya did not want to die, but of all the things to die for, Dominaria felt right.

"Who needs stone walls when you can hide behind an impenetrable barrier of screaming nightmares?"
—Braids

"Resist if you must. It makes no difference. As with Mirrodin, your world will bow to Phyrexia."
—Sheoldred
Before he was the Father of Machines, Yawgmoth was a twisted Thran physician, and his legacy of medical atrocities lives on in New Phyrexia.
To the merchant, it was nothing more than a few missing trinkets. To Tinybones, it was the greatest heist of all time.
"We cannot afford to let the Phyrexians win. They taste terrible."
"Lord Windgrace, grant me wisdom."
Backstabbing is common within demonic cults. So are front- and side-stabbing.
"Gix failed. I shall not."

"For some, perfection is but a single moment when form and purpose converge."
—Rona

"Ah yes, I remember that one. I turned him inside out and cast his soul into an endless nightmare a few centuries ago."
—Braids
Deep in the forgotten reaches of Urborg, ancient Phyrexian monstrosities shamble endlessly, putrid ichor leaking from their rusted forms.

"We sent three of our best legions! You're telling me no one came back?"
—Tori D'Avenant
Anger is his greatest weapon, and he sharpens it daily.

faces.f:
"That's not exactly what I had in mind when I said 'charge,' but I like your enthusiasm!"
—Balmor, battlemage captain
The drums and horns were expected, but the goblin dance was a pleasant surprise.
The rumor that contact with flowstone would reveal Phyrexian sleeper agents was spread mostly by Phyrexian sleeper agents.
The kavu adjusted easily to the Rathi overlay, incorporating the invasive flowstone into their own adaptable forms.
Minotaurs sometimes pretend to be lost in a battle rage, leading their opponents to underestimate their cleverness.
Countless generations of Shivan goblins have worked on the Mana Rig, giving them an unparalleled eye for useful relics.

"It's my fault, really. I told him to throw anything he could find at the enemy."
—Throppel, auxiliary commander
The magical echoes of the Hurloon mountain range greatly increase the potency of spells based on song or speech.

"For all their supposed advances, the Phyrexians still aren't fireproof."
—Jaya Ballard
Danitha watched in shock as electricity lanced from Jaya's fingertips, obliterating the charging Phyrexians. "What?" said the pyromancer serenely. "I told you I'd learned some new tricks."
Arrows fashioned from the living wood of Yavimaya carry all of the forest's rage in their fire-hardened points.
The cold snap killed off most of the heat-loving hellions . . . leaving only the strongest alive to breed.
There were many reasons why Shiv was not high on Sheoldred's list of places to conquer: big, fiery reasons.
